title: Decibels (dB)
summary: logarithmic ratios for power and voltage, plus the dBm absolute power reference.
body:
the decibel expresses a ratio on a log scale. power ratios use 10*log10, while
voltage (or current) ratios use 20*log10 because power goes as the square of
voltage. dBm is an absolute unit referenced to 1 mW into the system impedance.
examples: 0 dBm = 1 mW; +30 dBm = 1 W; -10 dBm = 0.1 mW.
an amplifier turning 10 mW into 100 mW has 10 * log10(100/10) = 10 dB gain.
gotchas: use 10*log for power, 20*log for voltage/current; mixing them up gives a 2x error in dB
dB is a ratio (dimensionless); dBm is absolute power -- do not treat them interchangeably
+3 dB doubles power but only raises voltage by ~41%
